'''Takahama Shrine''' (高浜神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Suita|en|Suita|qid=Q653510|lt=Suita}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}, Takahama Town<ref>{{ill|Settsu Province|en|Settsu Province|qid=Q864163|lt=Settsu Province}}, Shimashimo District (島下郡), [[Suita Village]] Takahama</ref>. The shrine's former Rank was that of a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

== History ==

[[File:Suita Takahama-jinja 2021-08 ac (3).jpg|thumb|Grounds and haiden]]

During the 5th century, in the era of the [[Yamato Court]], the local clan {{ill|Tsugita Muraji|ja|次田連}} crossed the {{ill|Yodo River|en|Yodo River|qid=Q1140505|lt=Yodo River}} and established the Tsugita Village, marking the beginning of Suita. The shrine originally enshrined the ancestral deities {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|Amenohoakari|qid=Q10940411|lt=Amaterasu-Kokutateru-Hiko-Honihimenomikoto}} ({{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}) and his son {{ill|Ame-no-Kaguyama|ja|天香山命|lt=Ama-Kaguyama-no-Mikoto}}, serving as the clan shrine of the Tsugita Muraji lineage. The name "Takahama" is an alternate name for Suita.

Under the administrative divisions of ancient Japan, most of Suita belonged to {{ill|Distrikto Miŝima|ja|三島郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishima District (Osaka)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10865943}}. After the {{ill|Taihō Code|en|Taihō Code|qid=Q1059892|lt=Taihō Code}} in 701 CE divided the Mishima District into Shimakami and Shimashimo Districts, Suita was assigned to Shimashimo District. To the north of Suita, the village of Fukui, also in Shimashimo District, is home to the {{ill|Niiya ni Masu Amateru Mitama Shrine|ja|新屋坐天照御魂神社}}, founded in the late 4th century by imperial decree of Emperors {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Sujin}} and {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Keikō}}. This shrine shares the same principal deity as Takahama Shrine, suggesting that {{ill|Nigihayahi|lt=Nigihayahi|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto|ja|饒速日尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}} was likely the tutelary deity of the Mishima District, including Suita.

The {{ill|Settsu Meisho Zue|ja|摂津名所図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Settsu Meisho Zue|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11498549}} states: "There are two shrines in Suita Village. They enshrine {{ill|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天皇}} and {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|ja|春日明神|lt=Kasuga Myōjin}}. These are the local tutelary deities, also called Myōjisha."

In 735 CE (7th year of {{ill|Tenpyō|en|Tenpyō|qid=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyō}}), the monk {{ill|Gyōki|en|Gyōki|qid=Q1136664|lt=Gyōki}} founded the Ishiura Jingūji temple to the west of the shrine, naming it Hamanodō (present-day {{ill|Jokoenmanji Temple|ja|常光円満寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōkō Enman-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11481316}}), making the shrine its guardian deity. {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}} ({{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞嗚大神}}) was enshrined at this time, and the shrine became known as Hamanomiya Gozu Tennōsha.
